question:
In a certain code language, 

‘P + Q’ means ‘P is the brother of Q’,

‘P - Q’ means ‘P is the daughter of Q’,

‘P × Q’ means ‘P is the wife of Q’ and

‘P ÷ Q’ means ‘ P is the son of Q’.

How is A related to E if ‘A + B - C × D ÷ E’?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aecbe9ab6b7da7cca1ac2d356e84b8c992ce57c8b50affd73dfdd3dad30ceb2e.png]

Given: A + B - C × D ÷ E

A is the brother of B, B is the daughter of C, C is the wife of D and D is the son of E.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/061d3723a72989c4a0e7f9706d64a2dda7c2437f5f66852f32e4c7b981b5b4db.png] 

So, A is the 'Son's son' of E.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
